key_insight: A lightweight lung tumor segmentation model reports a Dice score of 0.90812 with 430,052 parameters and 0.549 GMAC, targeting lower computational demands rather than drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: Efficient segmentation could support lung cancer assessment and treatment planning in resource-limited settings, but clinical utility is not established by the abstract.
method: Uses ENet with UNet-style encoder–decoder skip connections.
Adds Convolutional Block Attention Modules (CBAM) to improve feature representation.
Uses Grad-CAM to visualize prediction-relevant regions.
evidence_signal: Trained on TCIA data via the Medical Segmentation Decathlon and evaluated on LIDC-IDRI, the model achieved a Dice score of 0.90812 at a threshold of 0.5.
watch_item: Lower computational cost does not establish energy savings or clinical readiness; direct energy measurements and prospective workflow validation are needed.
paper_title: Energy Efficient Lung Tumor Segmentation with a modified CBAM ENet Skip Model
